title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with ring of integers A and residue field k of characteristic p. E_K is an elliptic curve over K, and T_p(E_K) (also called the p-divisible group E[p^∞]) is studied as an object over K. The page continues the case analysis of the previous page (good ordinary reduction, where T_p is an extension of L_K by its dual twisted by T_p(G_m)). It belongs to the 1966 letter to Tate, which compares an abelian variety over K with its p-divisible group.

(NB) Suppose j(E) is integral, so E has potentially good reduction. Grothendieck conjectures a p-adic analogue of the Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion: E_K has good reduction over A if and only if its p-divisible group E_K[p^∞] has good reduction, i.e. extends to a p-divisible group over A. The ℓ-adic criterion cannot be used here, since ℓ = p is the residue characteristic.

(c) Suppose j is not integral, i.e. potentially multiplicative reduction (Tate's case).
- After a finite extension of A, the identity component E_k° of the Néron model is a form of G_m.
- Hence the p^ν-torsion E[p^ν] contains a canonical finite subgroup that is a form of μ_{p^ν}.
- Passing to the limit, T_p(E_K) contains a rank-one submodule that is a form of T_p(G_m). It becomes Z_p(1) when k is separably closed, after a finite extension if needed.
- The quotient is canonically Z_p, because the Weil pairing gives det T_p(E_K) ≅ Z_p(1).
- So T_p(E_K) is an extension 0 → Z_p(1) → T_p(E_K) → Z_p → 0. Its class lies in Ext^1(Z_p, Z_p(1)) = H^1(K, Z_p(1)), which equals the p-adic completion of K* by Kummer theory.
- This completion is itself an extension of Z_p (coming from K*/A*, i.e. the valuation) by the completed units A**.
- The canonical element is Tate's period q, with v(q) = −v(j) > 0. Its nonzero image in Z_p is exactly what the previous page used to conclude that the extension does not come from p-divisible groups over A.

The page ends at 'Je conjecture'; the following page is headed 'Gribouillis de Tate sur sa théorie', i.e. notes on Tate's theory.
errors: Taken literally, 'E_k° est une forme de G_m' holds only for (potentially) multiplicative reduction after a suitable finite extension. With non-integral j the reduction over K itself can be additive, for example a ramified quadratic twist of a Tate curve. Grothendieck covers this with the bracket 'quitte à faire une ext. finie', so this is a gap in wording, not an error.
Without the extension, the sub Z_p(1) is only a Galois-stable form (a twist by a quadratic character). This is correctly flagged by the word 'forme'.

ideas.what: Conjecture: an elliptic curve (abelian variety) over K has good reduction iff its p-divisible group extends over A (p-adic Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion).
ideas.modern_name: p-adic good reduction criterion via p-divisible groups; later reformulated as crystallinity of T_p (Fontaine, Coleman–Iovita, Breuil)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (likely SGA 7, using semistable reduction and the monodromy pairing); crystalline form: Fontaine conjecture, proved by Coleman–Iovita 1999 and Breuil 2000
ideas.where_published: likely SGA 7 I, Exp. IX (§5), but I cannot confirm the exact statement

ideas.what: For potentially multiplicative reduction, T_p(E) is an extension of Z_p by Z_p(1), with class in the p-adic completion of K* given by the Tate parameter q; its valuation component is nonzero.
ideas.modern_name: Galois representation of the Tate curve; Kummer class of q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (unpublished 1959 manuscript); exposition in Serre, Abelian ℓ-adic representations (1968)
ideas.where_published: unsure (the Tate curve and monodromy are discussed in SGA 7 IX)

ideas.what: Canonical subgroup of E[p^ν] that is a form of μ_{p^ν}, coming from the toric identity component of the Néron model.
ideas.modern_name: connected/toric part of the p-divisible group, i.e. the finite part of the Néron model's torus
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. IX (orthogonality and the toric part)

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches Tate-curve theory and states the p-adic good reduction criterion as a conjecture in 1966. That criterion was soon settled, very likely by Grothendieck himself in SGA 7, and its crystalline form was proved later. The page is historically interesting as an early dated formulation, but nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above 'Néron' reads roughly '{+ de E +}' with a check-mark; it is probably 'modèle de Néron de E'.
In the bracket before 'Donc si k est', the line is better read as '[devenant isomorphe à T_p(G_m) dès que ... ]' (it is about when the form becomes trivial); the exact words are uncertain.
Near the end of line 12, 'T_p(G_m) = Z_p(1)' is a superscript annotation added beside the bracketed text, not a separate statement.
